data.long_meaning: Acacia (ἀκακία) is a name of Greek origin meaning “Thorny; the acacia tree”. From Greek ἀκακία (akakia), derived from ἀκίς (akis) 'point, thorn', referring to the thorny acacia plant. Its root is Greek ἀκακία (akakia), from ἄκη (ake) / ἀκίς (akis) 'point, thorn'. Acacia is a Greek plant name, not a Biblical personal name.

faq.q: Does Acacia appear in the Bible?
faq.a: No. The name does not occur in the Bible. The acacia tree (shittah) is mentioned in the Hebrew Bible, but the Greek-derived personal name is not a Biblical name.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Acacia verified?

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Acacia?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Acacia total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Acacia?
faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Akakia.

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Acacia?
faq.a: Acacia is transliterated as Akakía.

faq.q: How many syllables does Acacia have?
faq.a: Acacia has 3 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Acacia?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Acacia is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “Thorny; the acacia tree”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Acacia used today?
faq.a: Acacia circulates chiefly in Ancient Greek, English, Latin naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
